title: Countable saturation of a section-separating inverse system
statement: Let C be a small category in universe u, J a precoverage satisfying the site covering axioms [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and F a sheaf of sets valued in Type(max u w). For an object W and unequal sections s,s' in F(W), there exist a Type u nonempty directed partially ordered set I, a diagram U:I->C^op, an index i, and a morphism a:U_i->W such that the images of F(a)(s) and F(a)(s') in colim_I F(U_i) [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] are unequal. Moreover, for every finite J-covering family (V_k->X), every element of colim_I Hom(U_i,X) lies in the image of colim_I Hom(U_i,V_k) for some member k. Hom sets are lifted to the common universe u without changing their elements.

source.place: Tags 00YP and 00YQ: iterate the all-at-once refinement countably often to close the finite-cover lifting condition under new germs.

proof.text: Start with the singleton directed system at W. Its section colimit is F(W), so the two selected sections are distinct. For each directed system with two distinct section germs, apply lem-trf-point-system-refine-all and retain the new system, the order embedding, the equality of the restricted diagrams, and the two images. Choice and recursion on the natural numbers give systems I_n, diagrams U_n and embeddings e_n with U_n=e_n^*U_{n+1}. Every finite-cover germ from stage n lifts at stage n+1.

proof.text: Package the stages as a functor from the natural numbers to categories over C^op. Its Grothendieck construction G is small and filtered: two objects move into a common stage, whose directedness supplies a common successor; parallel arrows agree since G is thin. Define the union diagram on G by using the stage diagram on objects and transporting along the diagram equality before applying a fibre morphism. The functor laws follow from the naturality of these equalities. Mathlib identifies its colimit with the sequential colimit of the stage colimits. The comparison maps carry each stage coprojection to the union coprojection, and the comparisons commute with the refinement maps.

proof.text: The two stage germs form compatible sequences. If their images in the sequential colimit agreed, the filtered-colimit equality criterion would witness equality at one finite stage. The stage comparison is an isomorphism, contradicting the distinctness maintained there. Thus the original sections have distinct images in the union colimit.

proof.text: A Hom germ of the union has a representative at an object (n,i) of G. Regard it as a germ of the n-th system. Refinement at n+1 gives a representative b:U_{n+1,j}->V_k whose composite with the selected covering arrow represents its refined image. Compatibility of the stage-to-union maps carries this equality to the union, giving the desired finite-cover lift. The assertion includes the empty cover, where the existence of a germ would contradict the stage lifting property.

proof.text: The thin skeleton of G is a partially ordered type in the same universe. Its equivalence with G transports filteredness, hence nonemptiness and directedness. Precomposition along this equivalence induces isomorphisms on all the colimits. Transport the chosen root and arrow using the counit isomorphism. Naturality of colimit.pre transports the distinctness and every finite-cover lift. This yields the required directed poset system.

theorem exists_pointSystem_finiteCoverLifting
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : Precoverage C) (hJ : J.IsSiteForCoverings)
    (F : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type (max u w))) (W : C)
    (s s' : F.obj.obj (op W)) (hne : s ≠ s') :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : PartialOrder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirectedOrder I)
      (U : I ⥤ Cᵒᵖ) (i : I) (a : (U.obj i).unop ⟶ W),
      colimit.ι (U ⋙ F.obj) i (F.obj.map a.op s) ≠
        colimit.ι (U ⋙ F.obj) i (F.obj.map a.op s') ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (X : C) (V : Fin n → C) (f : ∀ k, V k ⟶ X),
        Presieve.ofArrows V f ∈ J X →
        ∀ x : colimit (U ⋙ uliftYoneda.{u}.obj X),
          ∃ (k : Fin n) (y : colimit (U ⋙ uliftYoneda.{u}.obj (V k))),
            colimMap (U.whiskerLeft (uliftYoneda.map (f k))) y = x
